text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on GENO-01: I re-ran every absence grep myself over all four files (wc -l gives 135/1103/415/1035 = 2688 lines, not 2689 — trivial). All 26 terms return 0: GWAS, genetic, genomic, variant, allele, gnomAD, 'Open Targets', ClinVar, GTEx, eQTL, LOEUF, colocali*, Mendelian, heritab*, 'odds ratio', 'effect size', 'p-value', biobank, 'loss-of-function', haploinsufficien*, DOI, PMID, PubMed, citation, reference. The 11 pLI hits are all substrings, confirmed. 'fetch' = 0 and 'XMLHttpRequest' = 0; I enumerated every URL in index.html/app.js and got exactly 5 distinct hosts (fonts.googleapis, fonts.gstatic, cdnjs, jsdelivr, alphafoldserver.com) with no API client — verified. The vendored-skills claim is verified and is in fact stronger than stated: `git ls-files` returns 235 tracked files, of which 229 are .agents/skills/** and only 6 are the project itself (.gitignore, README.md, app.js, index.html, skills-lock.json, styles.css); all 38 skills are keyed in skills-lock.json (I checked opentargets/gnomad/gtex/clinvar/encode/alphagenome/dbsnp/ensembl/human-protein-atlas — all PRESENT); none is referenced. I re-queried Open Targets myself (disease MONDO_0004975, associatedTargets Bs=[16 Ensembl IDs]) and every single score the reviewer quotes matches to three decimals: APP 0.872/gen 0.923, APOE 0.770/gen 0.889, ACHE 0.641/gen ABSENT, GRIN2A 0.623/gen ABSENT, TREM2 0.558/gen 0.862, GSK3B 0.554/gen ABSENT, CHRNA7 0.442, CHRM1 0.409, NTRK1 0.222, NOS3 0.187/gen 0.278, NTRK2 0.124/gen 0.080, NFE2L2 0.120, SLC1A2 0.112, KEAP1 0.088, PTAFR 0.085, FZD8 0.002/lit 0.015. I redid the portfolio arithmetic in python: 0.10/(0.25*2.6+0.75) = 7.14%, x2.6 = 18.57%, swing 11.43 points — exact. Two corrections force CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION rather than CONFIRMED, one of them material. First, the sentence 'no other platform target has AD anywhere in its genetic evidence' is contradicted by the reviewer's own data two sentences earlier (NOS3 gen 0.278, NTRK2 gen 0.080). Second and materially: the target inventory is incomplete. Reading FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA I count ~18 distinct declared binding-site targets, not 14 or 17, and the reviewer never queried six of them — APP/Aβ (app.js:278 'Aβ Oligomer Core (Lys28, Asp23)'; also app.js:158, app.js:334), ESR2 (app.js:352, 392), TJP1/OCLN (app.js:372), TLR4 (app.js:320), MAP1LC3B (app.js:330), AMPK (app.js:184). I ran them: APP genetic_association 0.923 — HIGHER than TREM2's 0.862 and the strongest in the whole set; TJP1 0.427; ESR2 0.227. So the headline statistic '1 of 17 (5.9%)' is wrong, and 'TREM2 is the one genetically validated target' is wrong: the platform's strongest genetically supported axis is Aβ/APP. The core finding — zero genetics layer, zero API calls, 38 unused vendored genomics skills — is unaffected and fully verified. One rhetorical overreach to trim: 'any reader who checks the file tree will reasonably assume the data flowed into the platform' is speculation; the README never mentions the skills, so no reader is actually misled by them. The verified fact (capability acquired, not used) is enough. Correction: Replace '1 of 17 distinct targets (5.9%)' and '13 of 14 named targets' with an inventory-complete figure. The platform declares ~18 distinct binding-site targets; at least six carry a non-zero AD genetic_association datatype score in Open Targets: APP 0.923, TREM2 0.862, TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227, NTRK2 0.080 (verified this session). Delete 'no other platform target has AD anywhere in its genetic evidence' — self-contradictory and false. Delete 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all.' Correct line total to 2688. Trim the 'reader checks the file tree' speculation. Pin resource versions (Open Targets release, gnomAD v4.1, GTEx v8) alongside the access date, since the report's own charge is unsourced numbers.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED on GENO-02: I verified every absence grep independently: 'indication', 'patient', 'placebo', 'endpoint', 'cohort', 'Phase I', 'MCI' all return 0 across all four files. I verified every quoted efficacy string at the cited line by reading the files: README.md:60 'CA1 LTP (+280%)', :67 '+240%', :71 'Information processing speed 2x', :74 'Synaptic ACh +350%', :84 '(+420%)', :88 'CBF +45%'; app.js:200 '+240% and sharpening operational focus'; app.js:240 'doubling cortical information processing speed'. All verbatim. README.md:22, index.html:7 and index.html:167 read as quoted. The disease-modifying/symptomatic/enhancement conflation is real and I confirmed it at the cited lines (app.js:188 Aβ/Tau clearance vs app.js:252 cholinesterase inhibition vs app.js:200 healthy-enhancement language). The load-bearing methodological point is correct and is core competence for this discipline: Minikel 2024's estimate is defined per target-INDICATION pair, so with no ontology term the strongest available prior on success is uncomputable in principle — I had to supply MONDO_0004975 myself to run any query at all, exactly as the reviewer reports. I tried to refute this finding as duplicative of GENO-01 and could not: a TPP is a distinct artefact and its absence independently blocks the analysis, so the concentration of two BLOCKERs is defensible rather than inflated. One unevidenced assertion to flag, not an error: the claim that cognitive-function/educational-attainment GWAS are 'massively polygenic with tiny per-locus effects and essentially no tractable single-target hits' is correct as far as I know but the reviewer retrieved no citation for it, while citing Bellenguez for the AD half of the same sentence. Either cite it or soften it. Correction: None to the substance. The cognitive-enhancement polygenicity claim needs a retrieved citation or should be softened to a stated professional judgement — every other assertion in this finding is line-verified.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on GENO-03: This finding is right in its conclusion and partly wrong in its reasoning, and one of its four sub-claims does not survive. Verified first: every quoted safety string exists verbatim at the cited line (app.js:167, 177, 209, 219, 271, 281, 291, 303, 323, 343), and I confirmed by grep that app.js:177 'Tumorigenicity: Negligible' is the ONLY tumorigenicity/oncogenicity/cancer statement in the entire repository — grep for tumor|oncogen|carcino|cancer|neoplas|malign returns exactly that one line. index.html:252 and :254 do diagram β-catenin stabilization → TCF/LEF → cyclin D1 as a therapeutic 'Outcome' with no liability note. I re-queried all constraint and association data. gnomAD v4: GRIN2A pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.277, obs 22 / exp 113.4 (80.6% depletion); NTRK2 pLI 1.0000, LOEUF 0.219, 13/94.5 (86.2%); GSK3B pLI 0.9999, LOEUF 0.409, 15/56.4 — all exact. Open Targets: GRIN2A genetic Landau-Kleffner 0.948, hereditary disease 0.877, Seizure 0.850, Rolandic 0.838 — exact; KEAP1 somatic lung adenocarcinoma 0.796, NSCLC 0.706; NFE2L2 somatic HCC 0.774, HNSCC 0.657; NTRK1 clinical NSCLC 0.948, melanoma somatic 0.608, HSAN4 genetic 0.941; NTRK2 clinical NSCLC 0.947, obesity/hyperphagia/dev-delay genetic 0.827, DEE 0.796 — all exact. Huppke 2017 retrieved and the quoted sentence is verbatim from the abstract. (1) KEAP1/NFE2L2: FULLY CONFIRMED and the strongest sub-claim in the whole review — three of 25 candidates (X3 app.js:161-168, M2 :307-314, M5 :337-344) engineer constitutive NRF2 activation; KEAP1 LoF and NFE2L2 GoF are recurrent somatic drivers, the germline experiment has been done (Huppke), and app.js:167 carries no oncogenicity field at all. This alone carries CRITICAL. (2) GSK-3β/Wnt: CONFIRMED. (3) GRIN2A: conclusion confirmed, reasoning incomplete. The reviewer did not do the domain-resolved allelic series their own argument requires. I retrieved Strehlow et al., Brain 142:80-92 (2019), PMID 30544257, DOI 10.1093/brain/awy304 (248 individuals): missense in TMD+linker → NMDAR gain-of-function → severe phenotypes, whereas missense in ATD and LBD, plus null variants → loss-of-function → milder phenotypes. The platform's declared binding site (app.js:216) is the N-terminal domain — i.e. the ATD, the LoF/milder arm — so the human allelic series at the platform's own domain does not predict the severe GoF epilepsy phenotype the reviewer invokes. The finding survives because 'Excitotoxicity: Safe' and 'Seizure Index: 0.02' are fabricated numbers on an archetypal epilepsy gene, but the inference is weaker than stated. (4) NTRK1/NTRK2: PARTIALLY REFUTED as framed, on three grounds. (a) The LoF-intolerance argument is mis-deployed: NTRK2 LOEUF 0.219 / pLI 1.0 means loss is not tolerated, which for an AGONIST programme is evidence FOR the direction, not against it — the reviewer's own literature entry frames LOEUF as bounding 'partial inhibition', which is not what these candidates do. That is a direction-of-effect error inside a finding about direction-of-effect errors. (b) TRK oncogenicity in humans arises from somatic gene fusions producing ligand-INDEPENDENT constitutive kinase activation; Drilon 2018 is a trial in fusion-positive tumours. Treating 'the approved oncology pharmacology is inhibition' as settling the direction question for ligand-mimetic agonism is a false dichotomy. (c) The human experiment has been run at the platform's exact anatomical target: I retrieved Rafii et al., JAMA Neurol 75:834-841 (2018), PMID 29582053, DOI 10.1001/jamaneurol.2018.0233 — AAV2-NGF stereotactically injected into the nucleus basalis of Meynert in 49 mild-to-moderate AD patients was 'safe and well-tolerated through 24 months' with no effect on ADAS-Cog. BasalNgf-TrkA-B3 (app.js:265-272) targets that same structure. The defensible criticism of B3 is that NGF/TrkA agonism in the NBM has already FAILED on efficacy in a randomised human trial the platform does not cite, not that it carries an unrecognised oncogenic liability. Finally, the reviewer under-states the real defect: I searched app.js and there is no code path anywhere that computes, derives or validates any safety, affinity or pLDDT value — all 25 safety fields are string literals, including the identical 'hERG IC50 > 50 μM' on every candidate. That is more damning than any direction-of-effect argument. Correction: Retitle to three programmes, not four: Keap1/Nrf2 (three candidates), GSK-3β/Wnt, and GRIN2A at reduced strength. Reframe the NTRK sub-claim: drop the LoF-intolerance argument entirely (wrong metric for an agonist), state that TRK oncogenicity is fusion-driven ligand-independent activation rather than evidence against physiological agonism, and replace it with the verifiable point that AAV2-NGF into the nucleus basalis of Meynert was already tested in AD and was safe but ineffective (Rafii 2018, PMID 29582053) — which the platform cites nowhere. For GRIN2A, add the domain-resolved allelic series (Strehlow 2019, PMID 30544257): the platform's declared NTD/ATD binding site is the loss-of-function, milder-phenotype arm, so state the residual objection as 'a fabricated seizure margin on an archetypal epilepsy gene' rather than 'the genetics predicts exactly this phenotype'. Extend the deletion instruction from the 7 listed strings to all 25 safety fields (app.js:147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395) — every one is a literal, and the uniform hERG value across chemically unrelated conjugates is itself proof of fabrication.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on GENO-04: I re-queried GTEx v8 median TPM myself via the v2 API and every number the reviewer reports is exact: NOS3 Cortex 4.288 / Hippocampus 2.243 / Spleen 75.479 / Lung 13.547; PTAFR Cortex 0.680 / Hippocampus 1.123 / Whole Blood 40.192 / Spleen 21.064; KEAP1 Cortex 29.066 / Muscle 88.333 / Artery-Tibial 37.826 / Lung 35.794; GSK3B Cortex 14.929 / Lung 19.305 / Artery-Tibial 16.054 / EBV 29.932; NTRK2 Cortex 74.242 / Artery-Tibial 37.531; ACHE Cortex 18.316 / Muscle 22.395; SLC1A2 Cortex 361.666 vs max non-brain Pancreas 6.049; CHRM1 Cortex 55.177 vs Prostate 25.642; GRIN2A Cortex 11.288 vs Testis 1.435; CHRNA7 Cortex 0.334. The CHRFAM7A point checks out exactly — I queried ENSG00000166664 and Open Targets returns approvedName 'CHRNA7 (exons 5-10) and FAM7A (exons A-E) fusion', the reviewer's quote verbatim. The absence greps (GTEx, single-cell, scRNA, transcriptom, Protein Atlas = 0) are verified. Three corrections, one of them material. (i) Arithmetic: PTAFR whole-blood/cortex is 40.192/0.679934 = 59.1x, not 57x. Conservative direction but wrong as printed. (ii) MATERIAL — the flagship A1 example attacks the wrong gene. AstroEos-NO-A1's declared binding site (app.js:352) is 'Estrogen Receptor-β (ER-β) LBD (Glu305, Arg346)'; eNOS/NOS3 appears only in the downstream mechanism string at app.js:356. The reviewer analysed NOS3 GTEx as though eNOS were the target. I ran the correct gene: ESR2 Brain-Cortex 0.098 TPM, Brain-Hippocampus 0.058 TPM, max non-brain Ovary 4.630 — ER-β is essentially absent from human cortex, 47x lower than ovary. The reviewer's conclusion is therefore right and substantially STRONGER than they argued, but reached through the wrong gene; the same applies to A5 (app.js:392). This is a correct-conclusion/wrong-reasoning case and must be fixed before issue, because a target-assignment error in a target-validation review is disqualifying on its own terms. (iii) Methodological: bulk GTEx median TPM ratios measure tissue composition, not in-vivo target engagement. NOS3's spleen signal reflects the spleen's high endothelial content — NOS3 is an endothelial gene and cerebral endothelium expresses it too — so 'a systemically administered eNOS stimulator engages peripheral vasculature far more than cerebral vasculature' follows from total vascular bed mass and BBB penetration, neither of which the reviewer analysed, not from a TPM ratio. The reviewer concedes the bulk-averaging problem in the ground_truth section and then uses the ratios as engagement estimates anyway. The PTAFR/A4 example is clean because PAFR IS the declared binding site (app.js:382), and KEAP1/GSK3B ubiquity is straightforwardly correct. The core finding — the five-region map is asserted with zero expression evidence and is contradicted for several targets — survives fully. Correction: Fix the PTAFR ratio to 59.1x. Replace the NOS3 analysis for A1/A5 with ESR2, the actually declared binding target: ESR2 Brain-Cortex 0.098 TPM, Brain-Hippocampus 0.058 TPM, max non-brain Ovary 4.630 (47x cortex) — near-absent from human cortex, which is a far stronger contradiction of the astrocyte/BMEC assignment than the NOS3 figures. Keep the NOS3 data as a note on the downstream mechanism claim, clearly separated from the binding-target analysis. State explicitly that bulk TPM ratios index tissue composition, not target engagement, and that peripheral-liability inference additionally requires vascular-bed mass and BBB penetration. Add TJP1 (A3's declared target, app.js:372): Cortex 22.13 vs Nerve-Tibial 99.08 and Artery-Tibial 60.36 — another ubiquitous, non-CNS-enriched target the review never assessed.

text: Verdict CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTION on GENO-05: The central factual claim is the single best-verified item in the review and I confirmed it digit for digit. I queried gnomAD v4 for 6-41161514-C-T: rsid rs75932628, transcript consequence TREM2 p.Arg47His missense; exome AC 4174 / AN 1,461,812 / AF 0.0028554; genome AC 304 / AN 152,342 / AF 0.0019955 — every figure matches the reviewer exactly. TREM2 constraint: pLI 7.9e-07, LOEUF 1.268, 20 observed vs 22.9 expected LoF (12.7% depletion) — exact, and correctly interpreted as LoF-tolerant/recessive-consistent. Open Targets TREM2 genetic_association: Nasu-Hakola 0.887, Alzheimer disease 0.858, frontotemporal dementia 0.666 — matches (minor: 'hereditary disease' 0.672 actually outranks FTD). I retrieved Jonsson 2013 and Guerreiro 2013 and both quoted passages are verbatim from the abstracts, including OR 2.92 (95% CI 2.09-4.09, P=3.42e-10), combined OR 2.90 (P=2.1e-12), 0.46% frequency in controls aged 85+, and cognition P=0.003 in non-demented carriers aged 80-100. The platform does name Arg47 as an agonist contact residue at app.js:300 and I confirmed 0 hits for R47H, rs75932628, Nasu-Hakola, stratification, genotype and biomarker anywhere in the repo. The catch is genuine and the generalised fix is the most valuable single recommendation in the review. Three corrections. (i) 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all' is false — I verified APP 0.923, TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227 and NTRK2 0.080 all carry AD genetic_association, and APP outranks TREM2. Same error as GENO-01. (ii) The load-bearing mechanistic premise — 'R47H sits in the ligand-binding surface of the TREM2 Ig-like domain and impairs ligand engagement' — is asserted with no retrieved citation. Guerreiro and Jonsson establish the association, not the binding-surface mechanism. It is well supported in the literature, but in a report whose central charge is unsourced assertion, an uncited structural premise carrying the whole 'the agonist may not bind in carriers' argument must be sourced or flagged. (iii) Framing gives the platform too much credit for specificity. Arg47/Asp87/Lys112 have no computational provenance — the whole array is hardcoded, three FASTA sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B' (app.js:130, 173, 371), and app.js:381's 'sequence' field is the English phrase 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'. The residue triple is decoration, and its collision with the target's most consequential coding variant is almost certainly coincidence, not a design decision with a stratification gap. The correct reading — that the platform named the single variant that made TREM2 a validated target without noticing — is evidence for GENO-01's thesis rather than a standalone stratification failure. Severity: I would lower this to MODERATE. It is a genuine and illuminating catch, but as written it is a corollary of GENO-01 applied to fabricated data, and MAJOR overstates a finding whose subject is a string literal. It should be retained and prominently placed, because the generalised fix is excellent. Correction: Delete 'TREM2 is the only platform target with AD in its genetic evidence at all' (refuted: APP 0.923 > TREM2 0.862, plus TJP1 0.427, NOS3 0.278, ESR2 0.227, NTRK2 0.080). Cite or flag the R47H ligand-binding-surface mechanism — Guerreiro and Jonsson establish association only. Reframe the finding: the residue triple has no provenance and the Arg47 collision is most likely coincidental, which makes it evidence that no genetics was consulted (GENO-01) rather than an unaddressed stratification decision on a real molecule. Note as corroboration that three sequences contain the non-standard residue 'B' and that app.js:381 substitutes an English phrase for a sequence.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: APOE is absent from the entire platform and the review never says so. APOE is the largest common-variant risk factor for late-onset AD (Open Targets AD genetic_association 0.889, verified) and the single most important stratification variable in modern AD trials, driving both efficacy expectations and ARIA-type safety management. It appears nowhere across 25 candidates, 8 natural products, 10 AF3 candidates or the five-region map. For a cognition portfolio this is a more glaring omission than any individual target's weak score.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: No tractability or modality analysis, which moots the entire regional-targeting discussion more directly than any expression argument. Every candidate is a 28-47-residue peptide bio-conjugate (app.js sequence fields), a size class with negligible passive blood-brain-barrier penetration, and not one candidate declares a transport or delivery strategy. The reviewer cites the Open Targets paper specifically for its tractability annotations and then never queries tractability or subcellular localisation for a single target. Whether a target is even reachable precedes whether it is genetically supported.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: FZD8 is scored nowhere despite being the review's own smoking gun. FZD8 has the platform's lowest AD association (0.002, literature 0.015 — verified, statistically indistinguishable from a random gene) and HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4 is the only candidate in the repository carrying an explicit tumorigenicity claim ('Tumorigenicity: Negligible', app.js:177 — I confirmed by grep this is the only tumor/oncogen/cancer string in all four files). A canonical Wnt agonist with essentially zero disease association and a self-asserted null oncogenicity claim is the cleanest single example in the portfolio, and the review quotes the string without ever evaluating the programme.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: No audit of whether the claimed binding residues correspond to the real proteins. TREM2 Arg47/Asp87/Lys112, GluN2A Glu201/Lys210, FZD8 Phe72/Tyr125/Asp99/Arg104, EAAT2 Thr368/Lys490 and the rest are asserted with no UniProt or PDB provenance anywhere in the repo. The reviewer credits the AChE residues as 'broadly consistent' but performs no systematic check — and their own excellent GENO-05 fix (surface ClinVar/gnomAD variants falling in any claimed binding site) is only implementable once residue numbering is validated against a reference sequence.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: Direct machine-checkable proof that the 'AlphaFold3' outputs are character-code art, which corroborates the whole fabrication thesis and was missed. app.js:381 sets the `sequence` field of AstroPafr-Block-A4 to the English phrase 'His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate'; that string is passed unchecked to initModal3DCanvas, renderModalPlddtChart and renderModalPaeHeatmap (app.js:649-651), so the modal renders a 37-residue pLDDT confidence curve and a PAE matrix computed from the character codes of hyphens and digits. Three other sequences (app.js:130, 173, 371) contain 'B', which is not a standard amino-acid code and which AlphaFold Server would reject. Two 'SMILES Formulation' fields contain molecular formulas rather than SMILES (app.js:60, app.js:70) and the curcumin SMILES at app.js:50 terminates in the invalid token 'OCH3'.

text: Missed by the primary reviewer: No versioning of the reviewer's own evidence. The review instructs the platform to stamp every panel with resource release version and access date (GENO-01 fix item 5) but pins none of its own numbers beyond 'accessed 2026-08-16'. LOEUF values differ between gnomAD v2/v4.0/v4.1, association scores change between Open Targets releases, and GTEx v8 has been superseded by v10 — all of which I had to assume rather than confirm from the report. In a review whose central charge is unsourced numbers, the report must meet its own standard.
